newsitem.title: RUSSIA: $1 bln Russia sales in few years - Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: $1 bln Russia sales in few years - Ericsson.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group LM Ericsson AB said on Monday it would reach $1 billion in sales in Russia "within a few years" and was considering investing in Russian telecoms holding company Svyazinvest.
"Because plans call for doubling (sales) every year, we will soon reach the $1 billion level," Ericsson president and CEO Lars Ramqvist told a news conference.
Ericsson officials said 1996 sales in Russia would reach $250 million, and could reach the planned level of $300 million. Sales in 1995 were $150 million.

"We will flat out around $1 billion," predicted Yngve Redling, president of Ericsson's Russian subsidiary Ericsson Corporatsiya AO. "Whether we reach that goal in 2000, 2001, or 2002 depends on the state of the Russian economy."
He said sales had been a bit slow around the June and July presidential election.

Ericsson controls about 60 percent of the mobile telephone infrastructure market in Russia, building cellular systems for providers, and sells roughly 30 percent of the telephones in the market, Redling said.
Ericsson sales world-wide are led by its mobile telecommunications, which are 80 percent of its Russian market activity, a company statement said.
